article.title: How Datadog Scales Its Agent to Monitor Millions of Hosts
article.full_text: Our infrastructure team walks through the architectural decisions behind Datadog Agent v7, covering Go runtime tuning, check scheduling, and how we maintain sub-second metric collection across 10M+ monitored hosts. Key challenges include goroutine pool management, JMX integration latency, and dynamic check lifecycle. Candidates who thrive here have built production systems under load and care deeply about observability.

expected.application_angle: Emphasize Go experience, distributed systems work, and any observability or metrics pipeline projects in resume/cover letter.
expected.interview_question: How does Datadog Agent manage concurrent metric collection without overwhelming host resources?

source.notes: Engineering blog with direct tech stack and culture signal.

article.title: How Stripe Engineers Think About API Design
article.full_text: Stripe's API has long been cited as a gold standard for developer experience. In this post, engineers from the Payments API team walk through the principles we use when designing new endpoints: versioning, backward compatibility, and ergonomics. We describe how new engineers onboard to our API design review process within their first 30 days, and how we balance speed with correctness.

expected.application_angle: Reference API design experience and knowledge of versioning/backward compatibility in cover letter. Mention any public APIs you've designed or contributed to.
expected.interview_question: How does Stripe balance introducing new API features with maintaining backward compatibility for existing integrations?

source.notes: Engineering blog reveals values and onboarding process.

article.title: Ramp Raises $150M Series D at $7.65B Valuation to Expand Its Finance Platform
article.full_text: Corporate card and expense management startup Ramp has raised $150 million in a Series D round, bringing its valuation to $7.65 billion. The company plans to use the funds to grow its engineering and product teams significantly over the next 18 months, with a focus on hiring senior and mid-level engineers as well as new graduate talent for its New York headquarters.

expected.application_angle: Reference Ramp's growth trajectory and your excitement to join at a scaling inflection point. Funding rounds mean headcount growth — mention eagerness to own features early.
expected.interview_question: What draws you to Ramp at this stage of the company's growth rather than a more established company?

source.notes: Funding announcement with explicit headcount growth signal.

article.title: Google's 2025 New Grad Hiring: What the Engineering Team Is Looking For
article.full_text: Google's early-in-career recruiting team shares what they evaluate in new graduate software engineer candidates, including system design fundamentals, coding proficiency, and cultural fit. Applications for the 2026 cohort open in September. Interviewers focus on problem decomposition, clean code under time pressure, and the ability to discuss trade-offs clearly. We value candidates who ask good clarifying questions.

expected.application_angle: Structure your interview prep around problem decomposition, trade-off discussion, and asking clarifying questions. Mention awareness of Google's interview format in your application narrative.
expected.interview_question: Walk me through how you would decompose a complex distributed caching problem before writing any code.

source.notes: Official career blog with explicit interview signal.

article.title: Why Jane Street Bets on OCaml
article.full_text: Jane Street's technology team explains why OCaml is central to our trading infrastructure, how we contribute to the OCaml open-source ecosystem, and what working in a functional programming environment looks like day-to-day. Candidates who thrive here tend to love types and correctness guarantees. We look for engineers who think carefully about invariants and program correctness before worrying about performance.

expected.application_angle: Lead with OCaml and functional programming experience prominently. Discuss type safety, correctness guarantees, and any open-source contributions to functional language ecosystems.
expected.interview_question: How does OCaml's type system help enforce correctness guarantees that would be harder to achieve in a dynamically-typed language?

source.notes: Official tech blog explicitly connecting tech choices to hiring signal.

article.title: Ramp Engineering: Building Reliable Financial Infrastructure at Scale
article.full_text: The Ramp engineering team shares how we think about reliability in fintech. Our services process millions of transactions per day, where a 0.1% error rate means thousands of failed payments. We discuss our approach to idempotency, distributed transactions, and our incident response culture. New engineers are expected to own a production service within their first 60 days.

expected.application_angle: Highlight ownership mentality and any production experience in your resume. Cover letter should address comfort with fast ownership and responsibility.
expected.interview_question: How would you design an idempotent payment processing system that handles duplicate requests safely?

source.notes: Engineering blog with culture signal around ownership and reliability.

article.title: Stripe's Engineering Principles: What We Optimize For
article.full_text: Stripe engineering is guided by four principles: correctness first, then reliability, then performance, then developer experience. We use code review to reinforce these priorities. New engineers are surprised by how much weight we give to correctness over velocity — we'd rather ship a week late than introduce a subtle concurrency bug. Our post-mortems are blameless and public to the whole engineering org.

expected.application_angle: Emphasize thoroughness and correctness in your cover letter. Mention any experience with code review, post-mortems, or blameless culture. Avoid framing yourself as a 'move fast' engineer.
expected.interview_question: Tell me about a time you caught a subtle bug in code review that others missed. What made you look more carefully?

source.notes: Engineering blog with explicit culture and values signal.

article.title: Jane Street Puzzle: Our Monthly Coding Challenges and What They Signal About Our Culture
article.full_text: Jane Street's monthly programming puzzles attract tens of thousands of solvers. We use them partly as a recruiting tool, but mostly because we genuinely love hard problems. Our engineering culture prizes people who find satisfaction in getting things exactly right rather than approximately right. If you've competed in ICPC, IOI, or similar contests, our interview process will feel familiar. We value correctness proofs over benchmarks.

expected.application_angle: Mention competitive programming background prominently. Reference Jane Street puzzles if you have solved them. Emphasize exact correctness and formal reasoning in your cover letter narrative.
expected.interview_question: Describe your approach to verifying that a solution is correct, not just that it passes test cases.

source.notes: Tech blog with explicit competitive programming and interview culture signal.
